root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before removeSession queues sentry->cleanupCallback as delayed work, the session's serverSubscriptions list must already be empty so the later delayed UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup callback cannot enqueue subscription delayed frees into the same delayedCallbacks list while that list is being drained.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original queues the second session cleanup callback while session2 still owns sub2. The fixed original deletes the subscriptions in removeSession before queueing sentry->cleanupCallback, so the queued delayed session cleanup runs with an empty serverSubscriptions list and no longer mutates the delayed-callback queue from inside UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup.

nodes.state: At the start of the second UA_WorkQueue_cleanup pass from UA_Server_delete, SIMPLEQ_FIRST(&wq->delayedCallbacks) still points at the already freed first-session cleanup callback, which is the AddressSanitizer-reported use-after-free read.
Deleting the live subscription from inside delayed session cleanup inserts &sub->delayedFreePointers at the head of server->workQueue.delayedCallbacks.
After SIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD removes the subscription delayed-free node instead of the iterator node, the loop frees dc even though dc is still the current delayedCallbacks head.

edges.relation: The same live subscription that remains on sentry->session.serverSubscriptions when removeSession queues the delayed session cleanup later becomes the sub object whose delayedFreePointers node is enqueued during UA_Session_deleteSubscription.

The subscription delayed-free node inserted at the head of delayedCallbacks during UA_Session_deleteSubscription is still the queue head at the next stale free iteration, so SIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD removes that inserted node instead of the iterator callback.
The first-session cleanup callback freed while still linked in the first cleanup pass is reread as the delayedCallbacks head at the start of the second cleanup pass from UA_Server_delete.
